label: Iowa · Story Co.
shows: Straightforward corn/soy rotation. The baseline everything else is read against.

label: Iowa · Clinton Co.
shows: Continuous corn. A clean single-crop season curve with no rotation to confuse it.

label: Kansas · rainfed
shows: Rainfed corn/soy. Lower peak NDVI than irrigated ground at the same latitude.

label: Maryland · cover cropped
shows: Cover crop running to planting. NDVI never reaches the residue floor, which is what broke minimum NDTI.

label: Georgia · El Dorado
shows: Boundary spanning two management units. CDL calls it split; the season curve is a blend of peanuts and cotton.

label: Georgia · Carpenter Rd
shows: Small cotton/peanut field under 7 ha. Tests whether the pipeline holds at the low end of field size.

label: Arkansas · rice
shows: Winter-flooded rice. Standing water makes cover crop undetectable rather than absent — the pipeline says so.

label: Texas · Lubbock pivot
shows: Continuous cotton on a centre pivot. Returns to bare ground every off-season; the cotton contrast case.

label: Washington · pivot
shows: Alfalfa and potatoes. A perennial stand the annual-crop model correctly refuses to date.

label: California · Central Valley
shows: Double cropping. Two cash crops in one calendar year breaks a single-peak season model.

label: Iowa · too-wide boundary
shows: A boundary drawn far too wide. The failure case the CDL purity check exists to catch.

label: Georgia - Mitchell Co. (no-till)
shows: Grower-confirmed conservation till with a cover crop. Spring armor 0.624 in 2020, the highest of the four Georgia fields. Pairs with the conventional field in the same county.

label: Georgia - Mitchell Co. (conventional)
shows: Grower-confirmed conventional till, no cover crop. Spring armor 0.488 in 2020. Residue is near-identical to its no-till pair (0.38 vs 0.39) - the gap is living cover (0.11 vs 0.23).

label: Georgia - Screven Co. (no-till, bare)
shows: Conservation till but NO cover crop, grower-confirmed. Armor 0.480 in 2020 - below both cover-cropped fields and level with the conventionally tilled one at 0.488. Conservation tillage on its own buys nothing measurable here.

label: Georgia - Jefferson Co. (tilled, cover)
shows: Conventional till WITH a cover crop, grower-confirmed. Armor 0.553 in 2021 - above both fields without a cover crop, despite the tillage pass. Phenology confidence is low for this field-year, so the window end is soft.

label: Colorado - Akron (wheat-fallow, wheat in even years)
shows: Dryland winter wheat-fallow, CDL Winter Wheat 2020/2022/2024 and Fallow 2021/2023/2025 at 100%. Tests the winter crop model (autumn sowing, May peak, late-June harvest), fallow periods of about 15 months, and 2026 read as wheat from the curve before CDL is published.

label: Colorado - Akron (wheat-fallow, wheat in odd years)
shows: The opposite phase (21.5 ha main block). 2026 has no crop in the NDVI and reads as fallow from the curve, with a post-harvest volunteer/weed flush in August 2025 flagged.
